title: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

endonym.native: Социјалистичка Федеративна Република Југославија / Socijalistička Federativna Republika Jugoslavija

capsule: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes — renamed Yugoslavia in 1929 — was founded at the end of World War I on December 1, 1918, uniting the former Habsburg South Slav lands with the Kingdoms of Serbia and Montenegro. King Alexander I declared a royal dictatorship in January 1929, abolished political parties, and imposed the name 'Yugoslavia', before his assassination in Marseille in October 1934. The state was invaded by the Axis powers in April 1941 and partitioned among Germany, Italy, Hungary, Bulgaria, and puppet states; Yugoslav Partisans under Josip Broz Tito reconstituted it as the Democratic Federal Yugoslavia in 1945, which became the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia — a socialist federation whose formal constitution was adopted in January 1946.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The interwar Yugoslavia's territory is precisely defined by post-WWI treaties (Trianon, Rapallo, Saint-Germain); the dataset's to date of 1946 reflects the socialist reorganization rather than territorial dissolution.
